ranking_basis: expected structural evidence gain against the validated drivers (mean K under dots, dot count, coverage, off-catalogue purity) and implementation cost. No DTI projection is made: the scored truth is login-walled and no holdout instrument for it exists in this checkout.

items.title: K-anchored consensus-support metric-marginal emission
layers: the 60 registry rasters (as the region definition only)
items.signature: mass-weighted mean K under emitted dots; dot count; coverage fraction
items.why_a_missed_fault: K highs with low U/K mark K-metasomatism / argillic-sericitic alteration along permeable structures, and in the northern Great Basin they also track young volcanic terrain hosting the geothermal systems the expert-added faults bound; the family's own score record says its higher-scoring rasters sat on higher K (+0.977; partial +0.913)
items.difference_from_repo: the repo used radiometrics as one input among many inside a prior field and never optimised the validated statistic directly; this session also restricted support to the six-best consensus region and used the published metric's first-order condition as the acceptance rule
items.expected_gain: MODERATE (direction validated in-family; magnitude unverifiable here)

items.title: Thermal-discharge corridor coverage (wells and springs as permeability evidence)
layers: GDR 1391 well/spring temperatures and thermal class (27,092 in-footprint samples; max temp 296.54 C, 1873 'Hot' rows)
GDR QFaults traces with slip rate and recency (126k CSV, CC-BY)
items.signature: corridor density between thermal-discharge points and mapped trace endpoints; gap segments of each trace that terminate near a thermal anomaly
items.why_a_missed_fault: geothermal systems require both heat and permeability, so the faults experts add in a geothermal prize are the ones that explain thermal anomalies; a trace that dies out before a boiling spring is a candidate for an unmapped continuation, which is exactly the class the catalogue is missing
items.difference_from_repo: the repo has never used the GDR well/spring table for placement (the manifest records that its label-derived dist_known_fault_px column must never be used); corridors add a *point-support* constraint that no prior family raster encoded
items.expected_gain: HIGH if the hidden faults are geothermal faults (mechanism is strong); testable in-family before any slot by checking whether thermal-corridor proximity of the dots raises the owner-score model's LOO fit
items.cost: LOW (CSV in hand; placement machinery already written)
items.risk: thermal springs also occur on mapped faults, so the signal must be gated to the off-catalogue domain; a well/spring 'Hot' class may simply re-find the map

items.title: Ternary radiometric alteration discrimination (K high, Th flat, U/K low)
layers: GeoDAWN K, Th, U, TC and the Th/K, U/K, U/Th extension bands
items.signature: K enrichment with Th conservation and U depletion, i.e. the radiometric ternary position of K-metasomatism versus potash/playa and versus mafic rock
items.why_a_missed_fault: it separates the *mechanism* of a K high (fluid alteration along a structure) from K highs with no structural meaning, which is what a K-only test cannot do
items.difference_from_repo: the repo measured single-layer dot means only, never the ternary/ratio structure
items.expected_gain: MODERATE — it mainly raises precision inside H66-1's support
items.named_non_fault_mimic: playa evaporites and agricultural potash raise K without alteration

items.title: Along-strike matched filter on the LiDAR scarp descriptor stack
layers: 12 lidar scarp bands: ex_max, ex_mean, step_max, lapneg_max, lappos_max, downface_max, upface_max, cross_max, relief, coh100, strike, valid
items.signature: coherent along-strike scarp amplitude with internally consistent downface direction and high orientation coherence at the 2-20 cell scale on a detrended surface
items.why_a_missed_fault: subtle scarps under young deposits and fan surfaces are exactly what expert compilers see in lidar and what bedrock mapping misses; orientation coherence is what separates a fault scarp from an isolated terrace riser
items.difference_from_repo: the repo used these bands as *point* statistics under dots; it never built an along-strike detector with a coherence gate, and the native-resolution scarplet/Steger method remains unimplemented (see the README deviation note)
items.expected_gain: MODERATE-HIGH (closest to the stated lane), but note the scale deviation: the mirror bands are 100 m aggregates of the 1 m descriptors, so this is a proxy
items.cost: MEDIUM (matched filter + coherence gate + spatial CV)
items.data_status: in hand, hash-verified; raw 1 m DEM not reachable from this sandbox

items.title: Competition-band structural corroboration (geodetic shear strain, seismicity, magnetics, gravity) folded into the K-anchored support
layers: the 19 organiser bands in training_features.tif (419 MB, 5 parts) — magnetics, gravity, geodetic strain, seismicity, MT, topography
items.signature: co-located shear-strain/inferred-dip lineaments with magnetic-gravity gradients; the family's own anchor already shows geod_shearrate partial rho +0.678 against score
items.why_a_missed_fault: active-strain and potential-field lineaments mark structures that, where geology is unmapped or covered, are the ones experts add
items.difference_from_repo: the repo's inherited runs used these bands through 100 m derived features, not as a corroboration term inside a K-anchored support
items.expected_gain: UNKNOWN — no local measurement of these bands exists yet in this session
items.cost: MEDIUM (419 MB fetch, hash-pinned and verified obtainable: python3 scripts/fetch_mirrors.py --only training_features)
items.data_status: obtainable (mirror confirmed reachable in this session via GitHub contents API)
